q: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
exp: Mass has only magnitude, making it a scalar quantity.
ai_exp:
Step-by-Step Analysis:

Step 1: Define scalar and vector quantities
• Scalar: Has only magnitude (size/amount)
• Vector: Has both magnitude AND direction

Step 2: Classify each option
• Velocity: Speed + direction = VECTOR ✗
• Force: Magnitude + direction = VECTOR ✗
• Mass: Only magnitude (e.g., 5 kg) = SCALAR ✓
• Acceleration: Rate of change of velocity = VECTOR ✗

Step 3: Verify
• Scalars: mass, time, temperature, speed, distance, energy
• Vectors: velocity, force, acceleration, displacement, momentum

Option A (Velocity): Requires direction ✗
Option B (Force): Requires direction ✗
Option C (Mass): No direction ✓ Correct!
Option D (Acceleration): Requires direction ✗

The correct answer is C) Mass.

q: What is the SI unit of electric current?
exp: The SI unit of electric current is the Ampere.
ai_exp:
Step-by-Step Analysis:

Step 1: Define electric current
• Electric current = rate of flow of electric charge
• Formula: I = Q/t

Step 2: Recall SI units
• Volt (V): Unit of potential difference/voltage
• Ampere (A): Unit of electric current
• Ohm (Ω): Unit of resistance
• Watt (W): Unit of power

Step 3: Match correctly
• Current → Ampere

Option A (Volt): Measures voltage ✗
Option B (Ampere): Measures current ✓ Correct!
Option C (Ohm): Measures resistance ✗
Option D (Watt): Measures power ✗

The correct answer is B) Ampere.

q: A car travels 120 km in 2 hours. What is its average speed?
ai_exp:
Step-by-Step Calculation:

Step 1: Recall the formula
• Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Step 2: Identify given values
• Distance = 120 km
• Time = 2 hours

Step 3: Apply the formula
• Speed = 120 ÷ 2
• Speed = 60 km/h

Step 4: Analyze wrong options
• Option A (30): 120 ÷ 4, used wrong time ✗
• Option B (60): 120 ÷ 2 = 60 ✓ Correct!
• Option C (120): Forgot to divide by time ✗
• Option D (240): 120 × 2, multiplied instead ✗

The correct answer is B) 60 km/h.

q: The acceleration due to gravity on Earth is approximately:
exp: Acceleration due to gravity on Earth is 9.8 m/s².
ai_exp:
Step-by-Step Analysis:

Step 1: Define gravitational acceleration
• Denoted by 'g'
• Pulls objects toward Earth's center
• Velocity increases by 9.8 m/s every second

Step 2: Recall standard values
• Earth: g = 9.8 m/s² (standard value)
• Moon: g = 1.6 m/s²
• Mars: g = 3.7 m/s²

Step 3: Analyze options
• Option A (5.0): Closer to Moon/Mars ✗
• Option B (9.8): Standard Earth value ✓ Correct!
• Option C (15.0): Too high, doesn't exist ✗
• Option D (20.0): Way too high ✗

The correct answer is B) 9.8 m/s².

q: Which law states that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction?
exp: Newton's Third Law states action-reaction pairs.
ai_exp:
Step-by-Step Analysis:

Step 1: Review Newton's Laws
• First Law (Inertia): Objects remain at rest or in motion unless acted upon
• Second Law: F = ma (Force equals mass times acceleration)
• Third Law: Action = Reaction (equal and opposite)

Step 2: Match the statement
• "For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction"
• This is Newton's THIRD Law

Step 3: Example
• Rocket propulsion: Gas pushed down → Rocket pushed up

Option A: Inertia ✗
Option B: F = ma ✗
Option C: Action-reaction ✓ Correct!
Option D: Gravitational force ✗

The correct answer is C) Newton's Third Law.

q: What is the frequency of a wave with a period of 0.5 seconds?
ai_exp:
Step-by-Step Calculation:

Step 1: Recall the relationship
• Frequency (f) = 1 / Period (T)
• Where f is in Hertz (Hz) and T is in seconds

Step 2: Identify given value
• Period (T) = 0.5 seconds

Step 3: Apply formula
• f = 1 / 0.5
• f = 2 Hz

Step 4: Analyze options
• Option A (0.5): Used period as frequency ✗
• Option B (1.0): 1/1, wrong ✗
• Option C (2.0): 1/0.5 = 2 ✓ Correct!
• Option D (5.0): Incorrect ✗

The correct answer is C) 2.0 Hz.

q: Which of the following is a good conductor of electricity?
exp: Copper is a metal and good conductor of electricity.
ai_exp:
Step-by-Step Analysis:

Step 1: Recall conductor properties
• Good conductors: Have free electrons
• Free electrons allow current flow

Step 2: Classify materials
• Metals (copper, silver, gold, aluminum): Conductors
• Rubber, glass, plastic: Insulators (electrons tightly bound)

Step 3: Analyze options
• Option A (Rubber): Insulator ✗
• Option B (Glass): Insulator ✗
• Option C (Copper): Excellent conductor ✓ Correct!
• Option D (Plastic): Insulator ✗

Copper is used in electrical wiring due to its conductivity.

The correct answer is C) Copper.

q: The energy possessed by a body due to its motion is called:
exp: Kinetic energy is the energy of motion.
ai_exp:
Step-by-Step Analysis:

Step 1: Define energy types
• Potential energy: Stored due to position (PE = mgh)
• Kinetic energy: Due to MOTION (KE = ½mv²)
• Chemical energy: Stored in chemical bonds
• Nuclear energy: Stored in atomic nucleus

Step 2: Match the description
• "Energy due to motion" = Kinetic energy

Step 3: Examples
• Moving car = kinetic
• Ball on a hill = potential

Option A: Position energy ✗
Option B: Motion energy ✓ Correct!
Option C: Bond energy ✗
Option D: Nuclear energy ✗

The correct answer is B) Kinetic energy.

q: What is the power of a device that uses 500 J of energy in 10 seconds?
ai_exp:
Step-by-Step Calculation:

Step 1: Recall power formula
• Power (P) = Energy (E) ÷ Time (t)
• Unit: Watts (W) = Joules/second

Step 2: Identify values
• E = 500 J
• t = 10 s

Step 3: Apply formula
• P = 500 ÷ 10
• P = 50 W

Step 4: Analyze options
• Option A (25): 500 ÷ 20, wrong time ✗
• Option B (50): 500 ÷ 10 = 50 ✓ Correct!
• Option C (100): 500 ÷ 5 ✗
• Option D (500): Forgot to divide ✗

The correct answer is B) 50 W.

q: Which electromagnetic wave has the shortest wavelength?
exp: Gamma rays have the shortest wavelength in the EM spectrum.
ai_exp:
Step-by-Step Analysis:

Step 1: Recall the EM spectrum order (longest to shortest wavelength):
Radio → Microwave → Infrared → Visible → UV → X-ray → Gamma

Step 2: Note the relationship
• Shorter wavelength = Higher frequency = Higher energy

Step 3: Identify shortest
• Gamma rays are at the far end with SHORTEST wavelength

Step 4: Analyze options
• Option A (Radio): Longest wavelength ✗
• Option B (Visible): Middle ✗
• Option C (X-ray): Short, but not shortest ✗
• Option D (Gamma): Shortest ✓ Correct!

The correct answer is D) Gamma rays.
